metadata.description: File System Command Dataset for OS Assistant

samples.question: I noticed that Yasser created a new file called "new_file.txt" under "/home/yasser/grad" on 2025-05-02. Can you help me list all files with the ".txt" extension in this directory and its subdirectories?
samples.expected_response:
Given that you recently created a new file named "new_file.txt" in your "/home/yasser/grad" directory on May 2nd, 2025, I can help you find all other .txt files within this directory and its subdirectories. To do so, use the following command tailored to your system:

   ```bash
   find /home/yasser/grad -type f -name "*.txt" | xargs ls -l
   ```

Here's a breakdown of the command for better understanding:
- `find` is used to search for files within a directory and its subdirectories.
- The `/home/yasser/grad` argument specifies the starting directory.
- The `-type f` option filters the results to only include files, as opposed to directories or other types of entries.
- `-name "*.txt"` filters the search results to only include files with the ".txt" extension.
- `| xargs ls -l` formats the output in a more readable way and displays additional information about each file such as permissions, ownership, size, etc.

By running this command, you'll be able to see all .txt files within your specified directory structure.

samples.question: Is it possible to see which directories are taking up the most space on my filesystem?
samples.expected_response: Yes, you can use the `du` (disk usage) command along with `sort` and `head` to find the directories consuming the most disk space. Here's a command that will display the top 10 directories by size:  ```bash sudo du -sh * | sort -hr | head -10 ``` This command will list all directories under your current location, sorted by size in human-readable format (KB, MB, GB), and show the top 10 largest directories.
